Actually "CCl" is a carbon with a chlorine attached, likely CH2Cl? In SMILES, "CCl" is a carbon attached to chlorine, with implicit hydrogens to satisfy valence, so CH3Cl? Actually carbon with one bond to Cl and one bond to aromatic carbon, so it's a benzylic carbon with one H and Cl: -CHCl-? Wait "CCl" attached to aromatic: "c(CCl)" means aromatic carbon attached to a carbon which is attached to Cl and has two hydrogens? The carbon has two bonds: one to aromatic carbon, one to Cl, so valence 4, so it has two hydrogens: CH2Cl attached to aromatic. So matches CH2Cl.
